sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.2% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $26.6 billion to $45.7 billion [F1][F10][F157].
The path was a step change, not a straight line: revenue climbed 25.6% in FY2018 and 23.9% in FY2021, then fell 15.6% in FY2024 and 11.7% in FY2025 [D93][D231][D367][D412].
The FY2018 step came largely from the Wirtgen acquisition, which added 12% to net sales for the year [P72].
Operating margin peaked at 21.2% in FY2023 and has since fallen to 17.5% in FY2024, while net income fell 29.2% in FY2025 to $5.03 billion [F29][F30][F40][D413].
Production Agriculture was the largest driver, at 37.1% of FY2025 revenue, but it fell 17.6% and subtracted 7.0pp from revenue growth [D657][D658][D659].
In Production & Precision Agriculture, sales volumes fell 30% in the U.S. and Canada, partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil [P10].
Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% and subtracted 3.0pp, while Financial Services grew to 13.8% of revenue [D889][D890][D891][D922].
Operating costs fell 7.3% against an 11.7% revenue decline, so operating costs fell 4.4pp less than revenue [D425][D412][D431].
EPS fell 27.8% in FY2025 against a 29.2% net income decline, as the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D415][D413][D427].
The FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% sat above the 12.1% window median but below the 21.2% FY2023 high [F30][D1335][D1334].
In FY2024 the margin fell 3.7pp, with SG&A costing 1.9pp and R&D 0.9pp [D378][D391][D390].
SG&A rose in FY2024 partly on a higher provision for credit losses, and R&D rose on continued technology investment [P33].
In FY2024 net margin of 13.7% sat 3.7pp below the 17.5% operating margin, with a 22.7% effective tax rate [F49][F30][D1373][D355].
Operating cash flow of $7.46 billion was 1.48x net income in FY2025, above the 1.17x window median [F80][F40][D401][D1364].
The FY2025 inflow was driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables, partly offset by an OPEB contribution [P5].
Free cash flow of $6.10 billion was a 13.4% margin, above the 11.6% window median, with capex at 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [F100][D398][D1341][D397][D403].
Cash and investments rose 13.0% to $8.28 billion in FY2025, while total assets fell 1.2% to $106 billion [D405][D428][F130][D419].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so net cash and debt-based ranks are omitted here [R9][X191].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.86 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow in FY2025, down from 73.9% in FY2024 [D409][D410][D365].
Return on average equity of 20.6% ranked in the 17th percentile against a 28.3% industrials peer median (n=6) [D411][D1361][D1362].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025, by 15.6% and 11.7% [R1][D367][D412].
Two consecutive double-digit declines mark a cyclical downturn in the core agriculture business, not a one-year dip [R1].
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [R2][D657][D658].
The largest segment shrinking fastest leaves the revenue base concentrated in its weakest market [R2].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so net cash and debt growth across the break are omitted [R9][X191].
Leverage cannot be assessed from this pack for the latest four years, which limits any balance-sheet conclusion [R9].
Whether Production Agriculture revenue in the FY2026 10-K recovers above the FY2025 level of $16.96 billion would confirm a turn in the largest segment [S95].
Whether the operating margin in the FY2026 10-K holds above the 12.1% window median or falls toward the 9.7% window low would show whether cost pressure is deepening [D1335][D1333].

Whether free cash flow margin in the FY2026 10-K stays above the 11.6% window median, against guidance for lower equipment-operations operating cash flow in 2026, would test the cash trend [D1341][P6].
